summary: Shasta-Trinity lookout on Grizzly Peak, staffed from 1912 or 1915 and rebuilt over time. Building reported removed by 2012, but a 2017 photo shows a structure.

facts.design: Lookout house on a five-foot block tower in its final 1953 form; the 1913 plan called for 12-by-12 houses with an eight-foot octagonal glass tower
facts.status_note: Vandalized building reported removed by 2012, but a 2017 photo shows a structure at the site; no source confirms its condition now.
facts.agency: U.S. Forest Service, Shasta-Trinity National Forest

visit.trail_note: Per a 2007 trip report, the lookout road is inaccessible because of snow until spring; current condition is unconfirmed.

notes_for_editor: Status unresolved: the register says a 2017 photo shows a structure; the Forest Lookouts page says the remains were removed in 2012; the 2007 trip report only passes on a rumor of demolition. Correction to 'unknown' proposed for a human to decide. Elevation: the register gives 6,240 ft (1,902 m), a 1913 item gives 6,800 ft; the record's 1,902 m is kept. Distance: the 1913 item gives twenty miles from McCloud and a 1915 Red Bluff item gives about fifteen; the story attributes the twenty-mile figure to the 1913 paper. Build date: the 1913 item describes new houses planned or under way and does not confirm a Grizzly Peak house finished in 1913; the register says since at least 1915. The 'Big Bend' location is from a 1923 item. A WebSearch found nothing on the site today beyond the 2007 rumor. Before publishing, confirm the current status with the McCloud Ranger District of the Shasta-Trinity National Forest. No photos found.
